answer:
**Orthogonal alignment rotates or reflects one coordinate system without changing its internal distances.** With paired row embeddings B from one encoder and A from another, seek an orthogonal matrix Omega making B times Omega close to A. This is appropriate only if their spaces differ approximately by that kind of transformation. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

Expand the squared Frobenius objective. Orthogonality makes the squared-norm terms constant, so minimizing error is equivalent to maximizing $\operatorname{tr}(\Omega^TB^TA)$. Take the SVD $B^TA=U\Sigma V^T$ and choose $\Omega=UV^T$.

**Why this is optimal.** Let $C=U^T\Omega V$, also orthogonal. The trace becomes $\sum_i\sigma_i C_{ii}$, at most the sum of singular values because each diagonal entry is at most one. Choosing C=I reaches that bound.

Center the paired data if translation must be removed, and restore the corresponding means at inference. Requiring a rotation without reflection needs a determinant correction. Test held-out retrieval: preserving distances within B does not prove that arbitrary changes in the encoders' semantics can be aligned.

**Technical details and references.**

With paired row matrices $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}$, solve $\min_{\Omega^T\Omega=I}\|A-B\Omega\|_F^2$. Expanding gives constant terms minus $2\operatorname{tr}(\Omega^TB^TA)$. Let $B^TA=U\Sigma V^T$; maximizing that trace yields $\Omega=UV^T$. Thus a new row embedding $b$ maps to $b\Omega$. [1](https://probml.github.io/pml-book/book2.html)

To see optimality, set $C=U^T\Omega V$, which is orthogonal. The trace is $\sum_i\sigma_i C_{ii}\leq\sum_i\sigma_i$, achieved at $C=I$. Reflections are allowed; requiring determinant +1 needs a sign correction on the smallest singular direction. Center paired data if translation matters, and apply the corresponding means during inference. The solution preserves distances under its map but cannot repair arbitrary semantic changes between encoders.
